summary: Per-action idempotency guidance for batched / multi-call function-calling requests
summary_detail: Customer runs a single chat turn that contains a batch of intended tool invocations (a multi-action response). They observe duplicate side-effects when the client retries at the request level. They want explicit guidance and a recommended pattern to achieve per-tool at-most-once semantics.
description:
Issue summary:
SonderAI calls Redwood with a single chat turn that asks the model to return an ordered list of separate actions (e.g., "[{call: \"create_ticket\", payload: {...}}, {call: \"send_email\", payload: {...}}]"). The model returns a multi-action response and the customer's runtime executes each action sequentially. When the initial request hits a transient network error, the customer's client library retries the whole request which causes the same set of tool calls to be executed again, producing duplicate side-effects.

Impact:
- Duplicate external side-effects (duplicate tickets, duplicate emails).
- Hard to dedupe because the actions are generated inside the model response (no built-in per-action idempotency token currently).
- Customer is using Dedicated tier and is sensitive to side-effect correctness.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (prod-us-east)
- SDKs: Python 1.8.2 and Node TS 2.0.1 in separate services
- Server runtime executes tool calls as HTTP webhook POSTs to internal services

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Send a chat request that instructs the model to produce multiple actions in a single structured response (JSON list).
2) Client receives response but the network connection fails before client ack; SDK retries the request at the HTTP level.
3) Backend returns same model response and the runtime executes the same sequence of tool calls again.

Observed behavior:
- Two tickets created in downstream system with different global IDs but same payload content.
- No per-action idempotency token present in the function_call objects returned by the model.

Expected behavior / ask:
- Guidance on recommended patterns (client + server + SDK) to ensure per-action at-most-once semantics when the model returns multiple actions in a single response.
- Suggested SDK changes or patterns to carry idempotency through retries without changing model generation prompts significantly.
steps_to_reproduce: Example prompt: 'Return a JSON array of actions to take. Each action is {name:string, args:object}.'
Run Python SDK call: client.chat.create(...) with prompt above and target model redwood-instruct-v1
Cut network immediately after first HTTP response to trigger a retry in the SDK (or simulate transient 5xx on first attempt).
Observe downstream actions executed twice by the service that consumes the model output.
logs_and_errors: Request ID: req-6a9f2b (first attempt) - HTTP 200 body: {actions: [{name:"create_ticket", args:{title:"..."}}, {name:"send_email", args:{...}}]}
Request ID: req-6a9f2b-retry (second attempt) - HTTP 200 body: identical actions array
Downstream system logs show two POSTs to /tickets separated by 3s with different downstream ids: ticket_1832, ticket_1840
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SDK-level retry replays whole model response which contains the action list. Customer does not currently supply per-action idempotency tokens in the generation prompt or in the action metadata.

Checked SDK behavior: both Python and TS SDKs retry transparently on idempotent HTTP errors; retries are at the request granularity and replay the same request body unless the application injects unique tokens.
Serving runtime: does not currently synthesize per-action dedupe tokens for list responses. Runtime exposes function_call payloads as-is to the customer's action execution layer.
Reproduced locally with a minimal script and confirmed duplicate side effects when retry occurs.

findings: No built-in per-action idempotency tokens are produced by the model by default when returning arrays of actions.
Customer replay occurs because SDK retries re-send the same request body and server responds identically; without unique per-action ids downstream cannot dedupe reliably.

Two practical mitigation strategies are available: 1) application-level per-action ids injected by the client at request time; 2) runtime/SDK-assisted tokenization where runtime returns stable call IDs alongside function_call objects.
recommended_solution: Short answer: adopt per-action idempotency tokens scoped to the action executor and generated by the client or SDK. Long answer and recommended pattern below:
recommended_steps: 1) Client-side: Before sending the chat request, generate deterministic per-action tokens. If you expect N actions, pre-create N stable uuids (call_uuid_1, call_uuid_2, ...). Include these tokens in the prompt so the model returns them embedded in each action object, e.g. {name:'create_ticket', token:'call_uuid_1', args:{...}}. This keeps tokens stable across retries.

2) Executor-side: When executing an action, persist an execution record keyed by (customer_id, action_name, token). If an execution with that token already exists, skip re-execution and return the stored result. This ensures idempotency even when the same model response is re-run.

3) SDK helper: Short-term you can implement a small helper that generates tokens and injects them into the prompt or into the top-level metadata field of the request. We'll follow up with an SDK feature suggestion below.

4) Alternative (runtime-assisted): For customers that cannot modify prompts, we recommend a small change: ask the runtime to return a per-action call_id alongside function_call objects. We've logged an internal feature request (INT-4021) to evaluate exposing stable call IDs from the serving runtime; this would let executors dedupe without client prompt changes.

5) Edge cases: If the model may reorder or merge actions, include both token + intended position index to make matching robust. If actions contain non-deterministic generated content, store a hash of the payload in the executor record as additional validation.
code_examples:
Python (client-side token injection):
from uuid import uuid4
call_tokens = [str(uuid4()) for _ in range(3)]
prompt = f'Return an array of actions. For each action include a token field that must match one of {call_tokens}.'
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-instruct-v1', messages=[{'role':'user','content':prompt}])
# executor can now use resp.actions[i]['token'] as dedupe key
Note: If the model doesn't include token field, use client-generated tokens and include them in the prompt in a predictable sequence so the model can echo them back.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Embedding tokens in prompts slightly changes model conditioning and could affect output format if not constrained; use explicit formatting instructions (e.g., JSON schema) to avoid drift.
If you pre-generate tokens but the model returns fewer actions than tokens provided, map tokens by position rather than name to avoid mismatches.
Runtime-assisted approach requires an internal change and rollout on Dedicated/private deployments — this is a longer-term fix.

Customer acknowledged they will test token-injection pattern in staging. If successful, they will roll to prod and close this ticket.
